rule: adjusted_score desc, total_score desc; dedupe by arXiv id / URL / id / title

papers.title: Whom Do AI Agents Work For? Role Assignment Induces Sponsorship Bias in LLM Recommenders
papers.summary: Changing who employs an assistant changes how it treats sponsored listings. Controlled hotel-choice experiments hold prices and reviews constant while varying delegation and sponsorship. In one condition, the sponsored-choice share differs by 22.2 percentage points between roles.
papers.key_insight: Delegation is a ranking variable. Hold candidates fixed and vary the principal and sponsorship label when auditing a conversational recommender; disclosure alone does not determine how the model treats paid placement.

papers.title: Beyond ICD Codes: Semantic IDs for Generative Medical Coding
papers.summary: SemICD replaces raw diagnosis codes with hierarchical semantic identifiers. It clusters code descriptions and trains bidirectional description-to-ID tasks. Across four LLMs and two medical datasets, Micro-F1 gains range from 1.34 to 8.00 points.
papers.key_insight: A useful identifier prefix should reflect task semantics. Bidirectional description/ID training gives discrete tokens meaning; the evidence here concerns medical coding, with identifier design offering the transferable idea.

papers.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
papers.authors: ['He, Bingxiang', 'Sun, Pengqi', 'Peng, Shihao', 'Li, Shaoxuan', 'Xiao, Huiyu', 'Shi, Hongjian', 'Fu, Zixuan', 'Qiao, Zi...
papers.summary: AutoSFT gives agents a broader action space for training-data research: reweight, prune, repair, replace and synthesize. Execution, analysis and synthesis have separate roles. Under fixed training conditions, analysis components raise the best IFEval score by 6.5 points.
papers.key_insight: Data research needs more options than mixture weights. For a recommendation assistant, rare-intent synthesis, label repair and duplicate removal can be separate actions, compared through retraining from the same base model each round.

papers.title: JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs
papers.authors: ['Zhu, Kunlun', 'Feng, Tao', 'Han, Xu', 'Wang, Heng', 'Yang, Ling', 'Tang, Xiangru', 'You, Jiaxuan', 'Ji, Heng']
papers.summary: JevAgentHarness delegates selected choices to a cheaper decision model and falls back to the LLM below calibrated thresholds. Training includes states reached after agent mistakes. On tasks similar to training, evaluated 4B models reduce agent cost by 81.1–89.0%.
papers.key_insight: Isolated decision accuracy does not predict end-to-end task success. Train on downstream states caused by mistakes and calibrate delegation thresholds on actual trajectories, where an inexpensive wrong choice can create costly rework.

papers.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
papers.authors: ['Sun, Bohan', 'Su, Zunhai', 'Zhuang, Xialie', 'Li, Jianjin', 'Wong, Ngai', 'Kuo, Chuan-Wei']
papers.summary: ReaDy reads a hybrid linear-attention model's recurrent state to provide position-specific context for a speculative drafter. Low-rank reads and fused operators limit overhead. On one B200, it achieves 3.16× mean decoding speedup over autoregressive Qwen3.8-27B.
papers.key_insight: Committed recurrent states offer context beyond the last hidden feature. For hybrid linear-attention serving, compare state-aware drafting against a hidden-feature-only drafter and measure whether longer acceptance offsets the extra memory traffic.

papers.title: Trajectory-Level Speculation with Semantic Verification for Tool-Using Agents
papers.summary: SpecAgent lets a small model draft grounded tool trajectories and a strong model verify whole segments. Read-only calls execute during drafting; mutations wait for review. On τ²-Bench, wall time is roughly halved while success stays within one point of the strong model.
papers.key_insight: Grounded trajectory review replaces repeated strong-model generation with parallel verification. A tool-using recommendation assistant would need to preserve real observations and place a verification boundary before external mutations.

papers.title: TreeSpark: Learning to Draft the Trees You Verify for Speculative Decoding
papers.authors: ['Zhao, Jihao', 'Jiang, Qianyu', 'Zu, Shuaishuai', 'Li, Pengfei', 'Fang, Guanghuan', 'Feng, Ben', 'Qin, Biao', 'Wang, Zh...
papers.summary: TreeSpark trains a drafter on the candidate trees its verifier will actually inspect. It replays expansion, pruning and budgeted packing using existing target distributions. Mean single-request throughput improves 15.1–25.0% over DSpark across evaluated targets and suites.
papers.key_insight: Train on the tree that survives inference, rather than only on a reference chain. Existing tree verifiers can reuse their branching budget and pruning policy during drafter training so supervision follows retained alternatives.

papers.title: Online Tokenization with Optimal Delay in Linear Time
papers.summary: This work streams the tokenization pipeline instead of waiting for each stage to finish a complete input. It formalizes output delay and supplies theoretical bounds plus practical implementations. Time to first token improves 7.9–34.8× over tiktoken in reported tests.
papers.key_insight: First-token delay and total throughput need separate budgets. Streaming query processing and long-document ingestion should measure both; approximately constant preprocessing memory also limits spikes from large inputs.

papers.title: One Block Ahead: Promoting Sampler State in Diffusion Language Models
papers.authors: ['Shen, Yangyi', 'Ku, Pin-Jui', 'Oswald, Nicolai', 'Lemercier, Jean-Marie', 'Fu, Yonggan', 'Ermon, Stefano', 'Leskovec, ...
papers.summary: One Block Ahead denoises the next text block alongside the current one. It promotes tokens together with their sampler state, including denoising time and self-conditioning. On DiffusionGemma, mean single-request denoising throughput rises 16.3% across ten benchmarks, with a small accuracy regression.
papers.key_insight: Parallel block generation must move sampler state along with tokens. The gain depends on the cost of a paired-block forward pass; the paper's break-even criterion connects local parallelism to actual latency.

papers.title: ixi-sLM: On-Device sLM for AI Call Agent Service
papers.authors: ['Lee, Han-Sang', 'Lee, Kyuho', 'Park, Juneyoung', 'Lee, Seongbae', 'Park, Jin Kyu', 'Kim, Minjae', 'Hong, Yuri', 'Lee, ...
papers.summary: ixi-sLM combines vocabulary trimming, a call-adapted tokenizer and task-aware mixed-precision quantization for mobile call assistance. One model powers call summarization and answering. The deployed model occupies 803 MiB and serves several million subscribers.
papers.key_insight: Vocabulary and output layers deserve their own memory budget. Frequency-based trimming and real-task quantization calibration can shrink both model storage and input length; this production report demonstrates the approach on mobile NPUs.

papers.title: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback
papers.authors: Li Wang, Chen Zhang, Yirong Yang, Xingyu Chen, Jinkun Zhao, Tianhao Peng, Wenjun Wu
papers.summary: Feedback mixes lasting preferences with one-off corrections. SkillGrain learns which atomic rules to retain and jointly trains skill induction and response generation. On one backbone, it improves the five-task average by 1.61 points over the strongest baseline.
papers.key_insight: Reward rule quality and retention separately. A correct correction can still be unsuitable for future requests; preference stores benefit from explicit scope.

papers.title: Bridging the Topological Divide: Dual-Branch Graph Distillation with Semantic Priors for Robust Cold-Start Recommendation
papers.summary: DualGCN gives interaction-free items a representation through semantic-anchored graph distillation. A separate student learns directions, while inference restores vector magnitude. On Sports cold items, Recall@20 exceeds DropoutNet by 20.8%.
papers.key_insight: Separate direction from magnitude: content predicts an item’s location more readily than its interaction-driven scale. The cold-only evaluation does not establish mixed-catalogue ranking quality.

papers.title: Revisiting Generative vs. Dense Retrieval: A Static Value Prior Reverses the Gap
papers.authors: Renbo Tu, Yang Liu, Shuying Sun
papers.summary: A controlled study separates exact-target recall, best-item value and whole-list value. A static value prior reverses generative retrieval’s apparent value lead; on industrial data it improves dense retrieval NDCG@50 by 11.8%.
papers.key_insight: Hold the popularity or value prior constant before attributing gains to personalization. Best-item value and whole-list relevance can favor different retrievers.

papers.title: PersEvalBench: Can LLM Evaluators Judge Contextually Appropriate Use of Persona Information?
papers.authors: Xinyi Liu, Hooshang Nayyeri, Emine Yilmaz, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Charith Peris, Hari Thadakamalla
papers.summary: PersEvalBench tests whether evaluators can judge the appropriate use of user history through controlled response pairs. On the human-audited subset, the strongest reported judge detects only 63.9% of under-personalization errors.
papers.key_insight: Distinguish omitted preferences from inappropriate reuse. These failures need opposite fixes, so an aggregate satisfaction score hides useful diagnostics.

papers.title: Learning Individual Scientific Taste with Privileged Hindsight Distillation
papers.authors: Hanwei Fan, Yanqiao Wang, Yiqi Zhu, Xuanyu Lei, Peng Li, Yang Liu
papers.summary: The study separates shared, evidence-grounded proposal assessments from individual preference mappings. Hindsight is available only during teacher training. The complete method reaches 0.693 on the reported real-researcher RW-SP metric.
papers.key_insight: Share factual assessment while personalizing trade-offs. Future evidence must remain outside inference inputs; the experiment focuses on research proposals rather than consumer recommendation.

papers.title: xLightGCN: Explainable Graph Neural Network Based Recommendation Systems with Most Influential Peers
papers.summary: xLightGCN decomposes LightGCN-family scores into influential graph peers and quantifies unexplained residuals. Gowalla experiments average each setting over 100 user-item pairs; larger explanation subgraphs cover more of the score.
papers.key_insight: Use the model’s actual computation as explanation evidence. Exact decomposition depends on linear propagation and does not extend directly to arbitrary recommenders.

papers.title: Calibration and Risk-Budgeted Decisions with System One Models
papers.summary: The paper calibrates binary decisions with risk budgets and conservative fallback actions. Across six moderation, safety and reranking datasets, Learn Then Test exceeds the target risk in 7.8% of settings with defined test risk.
papers.key_insight: Fit thresholds to the risk of the action actually taken. Calibration plots alone do not establish that an automated acceptance subset respects its error budget.

papers.title: MgRec: Multi-granularity intent interaction based sequential recommendation method
papers.summary: MgRec combines Transformer-based sequential preferences with coarse-grained intents extracted through a knowledge graph and a neural topic model. The publisher abstract claims stronger recommendations and reduced popularity bias without numerical results.
papers.key_insight: Keep recent behavior and broader intent as distinct signals before fusion. The accessible abstract does not establish the gain over simpler fusion baselines.

papers.title: Similarity-aware generalization framework for zero-shot cross-domain sequential recommendation
papers.summary: SAGERec selectively aligns semantically compatible items and adapts regularization to domain discrepancy for zero-shot cross-domain sequential recommendation. The publisher abstract reports gains but gives no numerical effect sizes.
papers.key_insight: Selective transfer preserves domain distinctions. Evidence is limited to the publisher abstract; the full page returned HTTP 403 and effect sizes could not be checked.

papers.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
papers.authors: Tong Zhu, Zhe Xu, Zefeng He, Yunkai Chai, Xuyang Hu
papers.summary: Intern-Decision returns structured closed-set choices and candidate probabilities in one causal forward pass. Its 4B model averages 90.02% accuracy across seven evaluation suites. These are decision tasks, not recommendation CTR experiments.
papers.key_insight: A compact choice model can support low-latency auxiliary judgments. Routing confidence still needs task-specific calibration.
